issues.body:
The `Value::Number` arm of `json_ld_equal_strict_order` (compact.rs:257-268) is a verbatim copy of the i64 / u64 / f64-fallback guard in `sparq_conformance::jsonld_bench::json_ld_equal_inner` (src/jsonld_bench.rs:60-78). The docstring at compact.rs:251-252 asserts the two "deliberately match", making array order the only difference — and I confirmed that is true TODAY. But nothing pins it. That guard has a documented change history (the sq-kk1mq numeric-guard added the >=2^53 exact-integer branch precisely so 9007199254740992 and 9007199254740993 stay distinct). If it is revised lib-side again, this test-local copy drifts, the strict score silently stops being a pure array-order refinement, and the docstring becomes false.

Impact is limited because the strict score is advisory and non-gating, so drift cannot produce a false green on the compact ratchet — hence minor, not major. But it is exactly the textual-drift class the crate elsewhere goes out of its way to kill structurally (see the jsonld_suite.rs:11-15 note on moving the floors lib-side to eliminate the #1463 floor-drift class), so it is worth closing the same way.
issues.fix_hint:
Preferred (structural, one comparator): thread the strictness through the existing lib-side recursion instead of copying it — `json_ld_equal_inner` already carries an `in_list: bool`; add a sibling `strict_arrays: bool` (or an `ArrayMode { Set, Sequence }`) and export `pub fn json_ld_equal_strict_order` from `jsonld_bench`, re-exported through `tests/jsonld_suite/common.rs` next to `json_ld_equal`. The numeric/string/object arms are then shared by construction and cannot drift.

Minimum (cheap): keep the local copy but add a parity test asserting the two comparators agree on numeric edge cases where arrays are not involved — `1` vs `1.0` (equal), `9007199254740992` vs `9007199254740993` (distinct under both), and a u64 value above `i64::MAX` — so a future lib-side guard change turns this test red.
issues.title: Numeric guard is duplicated from the lib-side comparator with no parity test, so the "deliberately matches json_ld_equal" doc claim can drift silently

issues.body:
The strict branch records a fixed string, `"compacted JSON differs under strict array ordering"` (compact.rs:223-226), with no indication of WHICH value diverged. The semantic branch immediately below (compact.rs:231-240) does the opposite: it truncates `got` and `want` to 240 chars and prints both, with the comment "Truncated got/want dumps keep a regression diagnosable from the failure log without re-running locally."

The whole point of this PR is to make an order regression "visible in job output" without a local re-run. A strict-only failure (the interesting case — semantic still passing, so no other lane reports anything) currently yields only a manifest id and a generic sentence, which is the least diagnosable failure in the file. Since the recorded strict count is currently 228/228, the first strict failure to appear will be a novel regression and precisely the one someone has to triage from CI logs alone.
issues.title: Strict failure message carries no got/want payload, undercutting the diagnostic purpose of the change

issues.body:
jsonld_suite.rs:155-157 says the line "makes an unmarked compacted-list order regression visible in job output." Strict positional comparison flags ANY array reordering, including ones JSON-LD genuinely treats as order-insignificant (multi-value terms, `@type` arrays, top-level node arrays). So a future strict-only delta is evidence of "an array order change somewhere", not specifically "a `@container: @list` order regression" — a reader triaging it could over-conclude. Today this is harmless because strict == semantic == 228, so any delta is a real change; the wording only misleads once the counts diverge legitimately.

The module-level doc in compact.rs:17-20 is more careful and does not have this problem.
issues.fix_hint: Soften to reflect what is actually measured, e.g.: "...makes an array-ORDER change (including an unmarked compacted-`@list` order regression) visible in job output. Strict ordering also flags reorderings JSON-LD treats as insignificant, so a divergence needs triage, not an automatic revert — at the current pin strict == semantic == the compact floor, so any divergence is a real change."
issues.title: The advisory comment overstates the specificity of the strict signal

verdict.summary:
Adds an advisory, non-gating order-sensitive ("strict") score alongside the gating JSON-LD-semantic compact score, printed as `TOTAL compact-strict <pass> <fail> <skip> (advisory)` with up to 40 diagnostics. Verified correct on the points that matter:

1. RATCHET SAFETY (the main risk): the only consumer of the compact score is ci.yml:2292 `grep -E '^TOTAL compact ' ... awk '{print $3}'`, and the infra sentinel at ci.yml:2285 `grep -qE '^TOTAL (toRdf|fromRdf|compact|frame|expand|flatten) '`. Both require a TRAILING SPACE after `compact`, so the new `TOTAL compact-strict` line cannot match either. A repo-wide sweep found no other consumer (only ci.yml). The new println is therefore genuinely advisory, as claimed.

2. REFINEMENT: `json_ld_equal_strict_order` is a strict refinement of `json_ld_equal` — positional array equality implies multiset equality, object comparison is identical (len + per-key lookup), and the numeric arm is a verbatim copy. So strict.pass <= semantic.pass always; the advisory number can never over-report.

3. SCORE ACCOUNTING: every manifest entry records exactly one of skip/pass/fail on BOTH scores (all six skip sites mirrored, all eight error paths mirrored via `why.clone()`, and the final compare records both), so pass+fail+skip totals agree between the two scores.

4. HONESTY: the amended docstring claim that the strict count "is recorded alongside the floor (see floors::compact)" checks out — src/floors/compact.rs states "strict-ordered count = 228", matching the gating 228. No overclaim; the diagnostic is explicitly labelled advisory in both the code comment and the printed line.

5. TEST VALIDITY: `strict_order_diagnostic_detects_unmarked_array_reordering` is non-vacuous — it pins the DIFFERENTIAL (json_ld_equal true, strict false) on the same input, so it goes red if either comparator collapses into the other.
